rich_summary: After a day of brutal carnage, both armies withdraw at sunset, their warriors blood‑soaked and exhausted. In the Kaurava camp, Duryodhana angrily rebukes Drona for failing to capture Yudhishthira despite his vow. Ashamed but resolute, Drona explains that as long as Arjuna and Krishna guard the Pandavas, victory is nearly impossible. He promises instead to slay a great Pandava hero and prepares an impenetrable battle formation, provided Arjuna is lured away. The Samsaptakas draw Arjuna to another front, allowing Drona’s plan to unfold. Abhimanyu, Arjuna’s young son, bravely penetrates the formidable circular array and devastates the Kaurava forces before being surrounded and killed by multiple warriors. His death brings jubilation to the Kauravas but grief and moral unease, prompting Dhritarashtra to question the righteousness of slaying such a youth.

highlight_spans.why: Vivid opening image of the battlefield carnage, establishing the brutal atmosphere of the war.
The defeated Kaurava warriors pass the night 'like men under a curse,' reflecting the psychological toll of the battle.
Drona’s crucial admission that no force can defeat the Pandavas while Arjuna and Krishna stand together, motivating the plan to draw Arjuna away.
The pivotal moment when Abhimanyu penetrates Drona’s supposedly impenetrable formation and begins his heroic assault.
Dhritarashtra’s grief and moral reflection on the killing of the young Abhimanyu.

top_scenes.scene_text: Young Abhimanyu charges alone into Drona’s radiant circular battle formation, his chariot breaking through ranks of armored warriors.
Six seasoned Kaurava warriors surrounding and attacking Abhimanyu simultaneously amid shattered chariots and dust.
After sunset, blood-covered warriors from both armies silently withdraw across a corpse-strewn battlefield as the sun sinks behind western hills.
